_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: The profile menu's keyboard selection stays visible as it scrolls. The screen is a 1280x800 desktop window. There are ten profiles, "Scroll-0" to "Scroll-9". "The input" is data-testid "message-input"; "the menu" is data-testid "profile-menu"; "the selection" is the menu's element with role "option" and aria-selected="true". "The selection is in view" means the selection's bounding box lies within that of its closest [role="listbox"] ancestor (top >= the listbox's top and bottom <= its bottom), checked with an eval re-run until it holds. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /new. Fill the input with "+Scroll". 2. The menu should hold exactly 10 elements with role "option", and it must scroll: its scrollHeight must be greater than its clientHeight. 3. With the input focused, press ArrowDown 9 times. The selection should contain the text "Scroll-9", and the selection should be in view. 4. Press ArrowDown once more: the selection should contain "Scroll-0" and be in view. 5. Press Enter: the input should have the value exactly "+Scroll-0 " (with a trailing space).

steps.expression: (() => { const sel = document.querySelector('[data-testid="profile-menu"] [role="option"][aria-selected="true"]'); const lb = sel.closest('[role="listbox"]'); const selR = sel.getBoundingClientRect(); const lbR = lb.getBoundingClientRect(); return selR.top >= lbR.top && selR.bottom <= lbR.bottom; })()
